root_cause_summary: DETERMINISTIC our-bug (corrected from earlier 'intermittent/environmental' reading). Full timeline from logs.gz: 11:13 first launch used DEFAULT workDir (C:\Users\86182\AppData\Roaming\AionUi\aionui) and aioncore started fine (all /api/assistants 200; user enabled assistants). Between 11:13-11:19 the user changed Settings > System work dir to the DRIVE ROOT 'D:\'; app quit 11:19:22. Every subsequent launch (11:19:24, 11:35:34, 12:12:08 - 3/3) failed ~3ms after start with 'BackendStartupError: aioncore startup directory preparation failed'. The D: drive was PRESENT and healthy the whole time - the app itself runs from D:\aionUI (app.asar, aioncore.exe load from D:). Root cause: documented Node.js Windows behavior - fs.mkdirSync on a drive root ALWAYS throws EPERM even with recursive:true and even when the drive exists (Windows CreateDirectory on a drive root returns ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, not EEXIST; Node's recursive mkdir only swallows EEXIST). ensureBackendStartupDirectory (introduced by PR #3536) therefore deterministically throws for any drive-root workDir, aborting backend startup on every launch. User was stuck in degraded mode (UI up, no backend, empty assistants), tried relaunching 3+ times (11:27/11:29/11:30 'Another instance is already running'), then filed feedback 'why do I have no assistant' at 12:13. NOT a disappearing-drive case.

introduced_by.author: piorpua (zynx)
introduced_by.original_intent: Fix: a missing configured work directory made Node's spawn cwd validation fail before aioncore could start. The fix mkdirSync's the startup dirs (incl. workDir) BEFORE spawn so cwd exists, and classifies the failure separately (localized dialog instead of installation-integrity dialog).
introduced_by.why_it_regresses_this_case: The fix assumed 'mkdir failed => directory unusable', but Windows drive roots are un-mkdir-able (always EPERM per Node docs) yet perfectly usable - they already exist. Any user who sets a drive root (D:\, E:\...) as work dir gets deterministic backend startup failure on every launch from then on. PR #3536 was verified on macOS only; macOS has no drive-root mkdir EPERM behavior, so this was untestable there.
introduced_by.code_ref: packages/web-host/src/backend-launcher.ts:365 (ensureBackendStartupDirectory) + :582-593 (spawn-stage try block) as introduced by a516ac5db

diagnostic_gap: The attached logs.gz records only the wrapped message 'aioncore startup directory preparation failed' with no causeMessage: the specific errno (ENOENT/EPERM/EACCES/ENOTDIR) and which of the 5 directories failed are not logged. makeStartupError receives the original error as cause, but it is not surfaced into the app log line. Cannot prove exactly which directory (most suspect: workDir=D:\ drive root) or which errno without that detail.

next_action: PRIMARY FIX (surgical, no product decision needed for this case): make ensureBackendStartupDirectory stat-first - if the path already exists as a directory, skip mkdirSync entirely. Drive root D:\ exists => skipped => spawn cwd valid => aioncore starts; per-conversation create_dir_all('D:\conversations\...') works fine because creating a SUBdirectory of a drive root is allowed. SECONDARY: (a) settings-time validation in updateSystemInfo/DirInputItem - warn or normalize when user picks a drive root or nonexistent path (resolveCliSafePath currently validates nothing); (b) add causeMessage + failing directory + errno to the startup-failure log and Sentry details (still missing; had it existed, this case would have been one-glance diagnosable); (c) the degrade design (workDir-only non-fatal + cwd fallback to dbPath + UI warning) remains worthwhile for the genuinely-absent-dir scenario (unplugged/network drive) but is a separate, rarer case than this one. Regression tests: ensureBackendStartupDirectory with existing dir / drive root (win32 mock) / creatable missing dir / uncreatable missing dir.
global_audit: Full-codebase audit (2026-07-28) for the fs.mkdir-on-drive-root class: ensureBackendStartupDirectory (backend-launcher.ts) was the ONLY unguarded direct-mkdir of a user-configurable directory. All other 11 mkdir call sites are safe: ensureDirectory (utils.ts:439) is lstat-first (#841); symlink targets + copyDirectoryRecursively + backup() are existsSync-guarded; initStorage/webuiConfig/configureConsoleLog/autoUpdaterService targets are app-owned paths or joined subpaths (subdir-of-drive-root mkdir is legal). Rust side (aioncore) is immune: std create_dir_all swallows any error when path.is_dir() (Err(_) if path.is_dir() => Ok arm) - a Node-vs-Rust behavior gap explains why only the Node side broke.
